Best-Fit Borrower: Business with consistent revenue and urgent capital need
Use of Funds: Short-term working capital; emergency cash gap; payroll bridge; inventory bridge
Minimum Readiness Signals: Consistent deposits; active business bank account; recent revenue history; ability to handle frequent payments
Red Flags: Thin margins; low average daily balance; existing stacked advances; irregular deposits; unclear use of funds
Documents Needed: Bank statements; business info; ownership info; revenue details; existing debt summary
Repayment Structure: Typically repaid from future revenue or sales activity; structure varies by provider
Broker Notes: Use carefully; may fit urgent short-term needs but can strain cash flow

Best-Fit Borrower: Business needing flexible access to capital over time
Use of Funds: Working capital; seasonal gaps; payroll timing; inventory cycles; repeat short-term needs
Minimum Readiness Signals: Stable revenue; decent credit profile; organized bank activity; manageable existing debt
Red Flags: Borrower wants to max it immediately; weak revenue; heavy overdrafts; no repayment discipline
Documents Needed: Bank statements; financials if required; business formation info; credit profile; debt schedule
Repayment Structure: Revolving access; borrower draws as needed and repays based on lender terms
Broker Notes: Best when borrower needs repeat access instead of one lump-sum fix
CTA / Next Best Action: Consider LOC if need is recurring

Best-Fit Borrower: Business purchasing or leasing equipment tied to revenue
Use of Funds: Vehicles; machinery; tools; medical equipment; kitchen equipment; production assets
Minimum Readiness Signals: Specific equipment identified; vendor quote or invoice; business use case; revenue to support payment
Red Flags: Borrower wants cash for non-equipment use; unclear asset value; equipment does not support revenue; poor documentation
Documents Needed: Equipment quote/invoice; business docs; bank statements; ownership info; possibly tax returns/financials
Repayment Structure: Usually fixed payments tied to financed equipment; terms vary by lender/provider
Broker Notes: Match equipment need to equipment financing before using working capital
CTA / Next Best Action: Collect equipment quote and route to equipment option

Best-Fit Borrower: B2B business waiting on unpaid invoices from customers
Use of Funds: Cash tied up in invoices; payroll before invoice collection; supplier payments; working capital bridge
Minimum Readiness Signals: Valid invoices; creditworthy customers; clear aging schedule; B2B revenue model
Red Flags: Consumer-facing business; disputed invoices; weak customer quality; invoices too old; concentrated customer risk
Documents Needed: Invoice aging report; invoices; customer details; bank statements; contracts or purchase orders if available
Repayment Structure: Advance against invoices or factoring structure; repayment tied to customer payment
Broker Notes: Strong fit when cash is trapped in receivables
CTA / Next Best Action: Request AR aging and invoice samples

Best-Fit Borrower: Business not ready for larger funding but wants to improve readiness over time
Use of Funds: Vendor accounts; reporting tradelines; secured credit tools; business credit setup; fundability preparation
Minimum Readiness Signals: Active entity; EIN; business bank account; willingness to build gradually; clean business information
Red Flags: Needs same-day funding; expects guaranteed credit lines; has no cash flow; wants shortcut instead of readiness work
Documents Needed: Business entity info; EIN; business address; bank account status; current credit profile; vendor/payment history
Repayment Structure: Smaller recurring payments or vendor account activity; structure varies by offer
CTA / Next Best Action: Route to credit builder checklist or nurture sequence

Best-Fit Borrower: Established business with stable cash flow and defined capital need
Use of Funds: Expansion; refinance; working capital; larger planned project; hiring; renovations
Minimum Readiness Signals: Stronger revenue; organized financials; acceptable credit profile; clear use of funds; repayment capacity
Red Flags: Urgent same-day need; unstable cash flow; weak documentation; high existing debt burden
Documents Needed: Bank statements; tax returns; P&L; balance sheet; debt schedule; business docs; ownership info
Repayment Structure: Usually fixed repayment over a defined term; terms vary by lender
Broker Notes: Better for borrowers who can document and wait

Best-Fit Borrower: Borrower with stronger profile, patience, and larger planned use of funds
Use of Funds: Expansion; equipment; real estate; refinance; working capital; acquisitions
Minimum Readiness Signals: Strong documentation; time in business; repayment capacity; acceptable credit; clean business records
Red Flags: Needs funds immediately; incomplete documents; weak financials; poor tax records; unrealistic timeline
Documents Needed: Tax returns; financial statements; use-of-funds summary; bank statements; ownership docs; debt schedule
Repayment Structure: Longer-term repayment structure; eligibility and terms vary by program/lender
Broker Notes: Strong option when borrower can wait and qualify

Best-Fit Borrower: Product-based business needing stock before revenue arrives
Use of Funds: Inventory purchase; seasonal stock; supplier payments; bulk orders; ecommerce scaling
Minimum Readiness Signals: Sales history; inventory demand; supplier invoice; clear sell-through plan; payout/revenue timing
Red Flags: Dead inventory; weak margins; no sales history; unclear demand; over-ordering; ad spend cash crunch
Documents Needed: Supplier invoices; sales reports; inventory plan; bank statements; platform payout history if applicable
Repayment Structure: Repayment tied to business cash flow or inventory cycle; structure varies
Urgency Fit: Medium urgency / seasonal or growth timing
Broker Notes: Best when inventory demand is real and cash timing is the issue
CTA / Next Best Action: Review inventory forecast and margin math

Best-Fit Borrower: Business with predictable revenue and growth need
Use of Funds: Growth capital; marketing; inventory; expansion; platform-driven sales
Minimum Readiness Signals: Consistent monthly revenue; growth signals; clear revenue source; repayment capacity
Red Flags: Unstable revenue; low margins; inflated projections; borrower treating it like free money
Documents Needed: Bank statements; sales reports; platform data if applicable; revenue history; business docs
Repayment Structure: Repayment often tied to revenue performance or fixed structure depending on provider
Broker Notes: Can fit growth-stage businesses if repayment matches real cash flow
CTA / Next Best Action: Compare against LOC/MCA based on repayment pressure
